data.name: Dhyut
data.gender_notes: Dhyut is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dhyut is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘dhyu’, meaning ‘to see’, ‘to observe’, or ‘to know’. In Hindu mythology, Dhyut represents the god of knowledge and light, illuminating the path to wisdom and truth. The name Dhyut carries the meaning “Knowledge, Light” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dhyut usually hope their child will grow to embody knowledge, light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of enlightenment and knowledge, guiding one towards wisdom and truth.
data.etymology: Dhyut belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Knowledge, Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dhyut total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dhyut carries a rich cultural legacy, rooted in the spiritual and intellectual traditions of Hinduism. It reflects the importance of knowledge, observation, and understanding in Hindu philosophy and mythology. The name is associated with wisdom, understanding, and illumination.
data.spiritual_significance: Dhyut is a name that resonates with the divine power of knowledge and enlightenment. It is said that the god Dhyut grants the understanding and insight required to traverse the spiritual path. The name is a reminder of the importance of seeking truth and knowledge, which ultimately leads to a deeper connection with the divine and a greater understanding of the universe.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Dhyut signifies 'radiant knowledge' or 'shining wisdom'. It is believed that individuals named Dhyut possess an inner light that illuminates their understanding of the world around them.

historical_references.reference: The sage Dhyutis mentioned in the ancient Indian text 'Atharva Veda' as one of the 'Rigvedic sages'. This text is estimated to have been composed between 1500-1200 BCE.

King Dhyutiman, also known as Dhutaka, is believed to have ruled the Gangaridhara kingdom in modern-day Bihar, India around the 11th century CE. He is notable for his military campaigns in defense of his kingdom.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's interconnected world, the name Dhyut continues to be cherished by Hindu families globally. The name bridges traditional Hindu values with modern Indian identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and cultural significance.
